text:
Connor McDavid has a point in every one of Edmonton's 18 games, 47 in all (10 goals, 37 assists), and the assists are the story. He opened the season with an NHL-record assist streak that had reached 14 games by Oct. 31, per NHL.com's Jon Lane, and 21 of his points have come on the power play. He's producing 6.62 points per 60 minutes, a pace nobody holds for a season, not even the man who just won his sixth Art Ross.

So what's real? The play-driving is. With him on the ice at five-on-five, Edmonton takes about 61% of the shot attempts and 61% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season. What isn't fully real: he's shooting 20% against 16% last season, and the Oilers have scored 17.4 more goals than their chances deserve with him out there.

Our range still projects 166 points over the full season (149 to 185), with that cooling built in. A quieter stretch is coming. It will probably still look like most players' best month.
headline: McDavid has a point in all 18 games
